name: OpenTripPlanner
tagline: Open-source multimodal trip planner with HTTP routing APIs
description: OpenTripPlanner (OTP) is an open-source multimodal journey planning engine that combines transit schedules (GTFS/GTFS-RT), OSM street data, and optional bike/car networks into a routing graph. When self-hosted (or via public demo instances), it exposes REST and GraphQL HTTP APIs for trip planning, stop/route lookups, and isochrones. Developers typically run their own OTP server; there is no single commercial multi-tenant API product with paid plans.

auth.details: No authentication required on the public IBI demo and typical self-hosted OTP servers. Production deployments may put OTP behind a reverse proxy, API gateway, or network ACL; OTP core does not ship a built-in API key or OAuth scheme.

pricing.free_tier_limits: Open-source software: unlimited use when self-hosted. Public demo instances are free but informal (no published quota).
pricing.paid_plans: None from the OTP project. Commercial hosting/support available from third parties (e.g. IBI Group / Conveyal ecosystem).

rate_limits: not published (self-hosted: operator-defined; public demos have no documented limits)
use_cases: plan a multimodal transit+walk itinerary between two lat/lon points
list nearby transit stops or routes for a map location
compute isochrones / travel-time polygons from a point
query real-time or scheduled trip options for a public-transport app
geocode-adjacent routing for last-mile bike or micromobility legs
